component.name: Sharpr
component.summary: Fast image quality review for Linux

description.p: Sharpr is a fast, local-first image quality review tool for Linux. Open a folder, move through the filmstrip, decide what to keep, compare similar images, tag and collect the keepers, and send export or upscale work through Tasks. Folders are the source of truth; Sharpr never modifies your original files.

Features include a GNOME-native three-pane layout, SQLite-backed library index, collections with tag inheritance, duplicate detection, resolution-based quality scoring, export to JPEG/PNG/WebP/JXL, and optional AI upscaling via local ONNX models or a configurable ComfyUI backend.

screenshot.caption: Three-pane image browser showing the folder sidebar, filmstrip, and viewer.

description.p: SQLite library index, tags and collections with tag inheritance, duplicate detection via dHash, resolution-based quality scoring, export pipeline (JPEG/PNG/WebP/JXL), AI upscaling via ONNX and ComfyUI backends, Tasks dashboard, compare page, and presentation mode.
Initial MVP release: three-pane adaptive UI, thumbnail filmstrip, image preview, metadata overlay.
